module_title: The Solar System and Earth's Structure - Basic Understanding
introduction: The study of Geography begins with understanding our cosmic neighborhood and the very planet we live on. The Solar System is a family consisting of the Sun and 8 planets gravitationally bound to it. At this level, we will memorize the basic characteristics of the planets and the foundational names of Earth's internal layers.

core_concepts.title: The Sun
core_concepts.description: The Sun is the center of our solar system and the ultimate source of energy. It is composed primarily of Hydrogen (approx. 71%) and Helium (approx. 26.5%). The massive energy of the Sun is generated through a process called 'Nuclear Fusion'.

core_concepts.title: Order of the Planets
core_concepts.description: There are 8 planets in order of their distance from the Sun: 1. Mercury, 2. Venus, 3. Earth, 4. Mars, 5. Jupiter, 6. Saturn, 7. Uranus, 8. Neptune.

core_concepts.title: Earth's Internal Structure
core_concepts.description: The Earth is structured somewhat like an onion, primarily consisting of three concentric layers: 1. Crust - The outermost, thinnest solid layer. 2. Mantle - The middle and thickest layer. 3. Core - The innermost and hottest part of the Earth.

core_concepts.title: The Largest and Smallest Planets
core_concepts.description: 'Jupiter' is the undisputed largest planet in the solar system (both in size and mass). 'Mercury' is the smallest planet and the one closest to the Sun.

important_entities.name: Venus
important_entities.key_fact: The Hottest Planet and Earth's Twin
important_entities.significance: Even though Mercury is closest to the Sun, 'Venus' is the hottest planet in the solar system. This is because Venus has a thick atmosphere composed of 96% Carbon Dioxide (CO2), creating a runaway 'Greenhouse Effect'. It is also called the 'Morning Star' and 'Evening Star'.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Students logically assume that 'Mercury' must be the hottest because it is closest to the Sun. This is a trap. Mercury has no atmosphere to trap the heat. 'Venus' is the hottest planet due to its dense, heat-trapping CO2 atmosphere.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: My Very Educated Mother Just Served Us Noodles
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: M(Mercury), V(Venus), E(Earth), M(Mars), J(Jupiter), S(Saturn), U(Uranus), N(Neptune).

exam_strategy_tips: If an exam asks for 'Earth's Twin', always choose 'Venus' because its size and mass are incredibly similar to Earth's.
The source of the Sun's energy ('Nuclear Fusion') is a highly repeated question in both Geography and basic Physics exams.
